title: He Fell 22,000 Feet With No Parachute and Landed on a Glass Roof

scenes.text: In 1943, a man fell four miles without a parachute. And lived.
Alan Magee was a B-17 gunner. His bomber was hit over France, and he fell out at 22,000 feet.
He crashed through the glass roof of a train station. The glass broke his fall.
He had 28 shrapnel wounds and a punctured lung. But he was alive.
He lived to be 84. A four mile fall, ended by a window.

description:
In January 1943, B-17 gunner Alan Magee fell about 22,000 feet without a parachute and survived.
He crashed through the glass roof of the Saint-Nazaire train station in France, which absorbed much of the impact. He suffered 28 shrapnel wounds and many other injuries, was treated by German doctors and spent the rest of the war as a prisoner. He died in 2003 at age 84.
Could you have survived this? Comment below.
first_comment: The glass roof is why he lived: it absorbed a lot of the force. Is that luck, or the luckiest roof in history?
